text:
For most healthy adults, a low-carbohydrate diet is safe in the short to medium term and often helps with weight loss and blood sugar control, though it can cause fatigue, headache, and constipation early on and may leave gaps in fiber and micronutrients unless planned well. Because carbohydrate supplies the glycogen that fuels high-intensity exercise, very low intake can impair performance in that kind of training, although the body adapts over several weeks. Long-term effects are still debated, so people with diabetes on medication, kidney disease, or other conditions should check with a clinician first.
